title: Explicit conjugation identities for tensor resolution comparisons
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-étale site, small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the pulled-back ring object $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and the fixed exact internal/section module equivalence $E_T$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary operations and universe convention of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Let $q_T^{\mathrm i},q_T^{\mathrm s}$ denote the internal and section homotopy-to-derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm i},\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm s}$ for the full subcategories of K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with the corresponding exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests internally. All total tensors below are signed direct-sum cochain totals [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and all derived tensors are relative to $R_T$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $F=f^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and $LF$ the specified total derived section pullback with comparison $\epsilon_A:LF(q_Y^{\mathrm s}A)\to q_X^{\mathrm s}(FA)$ of [def-pd-section-derived-realization]. Use the derived pullback comparison $\gamma:D(E_X)Lf^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong LF D(E_Y)$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization], compatible with these resolution transformations, and the normalized $\theta_T,e_T$ of [lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison]. Write $F_{\mathrm i}=f^*_{\mathrm{int}}$, $L_{\mathrm i}=Lf^*_{\mathrm{int}}$, $G_T=D(E_T)$, and $\eta_A:L_{\mathrm i}q_Y^{\mathrm i}A\to q_X^{\mathrm i}F_{\mathrm i}A$ for the internal resolution transformation. Let $h_A:E_XF_{\mathrm i}A\cong FE_YA$ be the ordinary comparison, $t_{T;A,B}:E_T\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(E_TA\otimes E_TB)$ the signed-total comparison, and $\kappa_A:G_Tq_T^{\mathrm i}A\cong q_T^{\mathrm s}E_TA$ the localization factor [def-pd-section-derived-tensor-data]. For internal resolving $A,B$ put $P=E_YA$, $Q=E_YB$, $Z=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B)$ and $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$. Let $r_T^{\mathrm i},r_T^{\mathrm s}$ be the prescribed representative tensor maps, $r_T^{\mathrm s}$ being the ringed representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Set
$$d_A=q_X^{\mathrm s}(h_A)\kappa_{F_{\mathrm i}A},\quad d_Z=q_X^{\mathrm s}(Ft_{Y;A,B})q_X^{\mathrm s}(h_Z)\kappa_{F_{\mathrm i}Z},$$
$$d_{\rm out}=q_X^{\mathrm s}(\operatorname{Tot}(h_A\otimes h_B))q_X^{\mathrm s}(t_{X;F_{\mathrm i}A,F_{\mathrm i}B})\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(F_{\mathrm i}A\otimes F_{\mathrm i}B)}.$$
Define the input identifications
$$j_A=LF(\kappa_A)\gamma_{q_Y^{\mathrm i}A},\quad j_{AB}=LF((\kappa_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa_B)\theta_{Y;q_Y^{\mathrm i}A,q_Y^{\mathrm i}B})\gamma_{q_Y^{\mathrm i}A\otimes^{\mathbf L}q_Y^{\mathrm i}B},$$
and the output identification
$$k_{AB}=(LF(\kappa_A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}LF(\kappa_B))(\gamma_{q_Y^{\mathrm i}A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\gamma_{q_Y^{\mathrm i}B})\theta_{X;L_{\mathrm i}q_Y^{\mathrm i}A,L_{\mathrm i}q_Y^{\mathrm i}B}.$$
Put $a^{\mathrm i}=\eta_ZL_{\mathrm i}((r_Y^{\mathrm i})^{-1})$, $c^{\mathrm i}=(r_X^{\mathrm i})^{-1}(\eta_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\eta_B)$, $a^{\mathrm s}=\epsilon_VLF((r_Y^{\mathrm s})^{-1})$ and $c^{\mathrm s}=(r_X^{\mathrm s})^{-1}(\epsilon_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_Q)$. Then the following identities hold in the section-derived category:
$$d_AG_X(\eta_A)=\epsilon_Pj_A,\qquad d_ZG_X(a^{\mathrm i})=a^{\mathrm s}j_{AB},\qquad d_{\rm out}G_X(c^{\mathrm i})=c^{\mathrm s}k_{AB}.$$
For the actual internal and section total arrows $b^{\mathrm i},b^{\mathrm s}$ [lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison] one also has
$$d_{\rm out}G_Xq_X^{\mathrm i}(b^{\mathrm i}_{A,B})=q_X^{\mathrm s}(b^{\mathrm s}_{P,Q})d_Z.$$
For units let $\ell_T:E_T(R_T[0])\cong R_{T,\mathrm{sec}}[0]$ be the ordinary regular-module comparison, let $u^{\mathrm i}$ be the internal total unit and $u^{\mathrm s}$ ordinary scalar multiplication. With $e_T=q_T^{\mathrm s}(\ell_T)\kappa_{R_T[0]}$, the unary identity is
$$e_XG_X(q_X^{\mathrm i}(u^{\mathrm i})\eta_{R_Y[0]})=q_X^{\mathrm s}(u^{\mathrm s})\epsilon_{R_{Y,\mathrm{sec}}[0]}LF(e_Y)\gamma_{R_Y[0]}.$$
All these equations are natural on resolving complexes. Every resolving section complex is isomorphic to an image $E_TA$ of a resolving internal complex, and substitution along the equivalence counit isomorphisms preserves these equations. The identities identify the specified comparison factors, without asserting or assuming any equality between independently constructed derived pullback tensor transformations.

proof.text: Write out the resolution-compatibility clause of sectionDerivedPushpullNormalization. Its reverse is the unary equation, with eta, epsilon, d and j unfolded. This works for every internal complex.

Use qTensorArrow_normalization, the canonical component form of the existing all-complex TensorRepresentativeCondition. It cancels the inverse localization and tensor factors without changing any map. Naturality of gamma at mu, the unary equation at the total tensor, and epsilon-naturality at the ordinary total comparison give the input equation. The component interfaces cochainLocalizationIso and derivedSectionTensorIso are the original κ and θ with canonical component types. Read the stored forward map of sectionConjugationIso directly; cancel its first two inverse factors using functoriality, without rebuilding a chain of isomorphism compositions.

Apply the same representative identity at the internal pullbacks of the two complexes. Use naturality of qTensor at the two termwise pullback isomorphisms, naturality of tensorComparison at the two eta maps, and the two unary equations. Bifunctoriality combines each of the three pairs of factors to give exactly kTensor followed by cSection. No resolving-preservation assertion is needed, because TensorRepresentativeCondition is stated for all complexes.

Use the ordinary forward-map and unit clauses of section_oplax_total_comparison. Precompose the forward-map identity with the two invertible source transports, localize it, and paste it with naturality of the localization factor kappa. This is the total-arrow equation. The analogous unit cancellation, followed by the unary equation at the internal unit and epsilon-naturality at the ordinary unit comparison, gives UnitEquation.

Use the naturality API of the canonically typed cochainTensorComparison. Paste it with naturality of the localization factor kappa, the termwise pullback comparison, eta and the actual internal total oplax map to prove all four Naturality squares. The comparison API proves its naturality from the original pure-tensor and summand characterizations, retaining the specified maps. The Lean calculation uses generic square-pasting lemmas and applies the comparison naturality APIs explicitly.

Naturality of epsilon, qTensor and the section total oplax map transports Equations along arbitrary section-complex isomorphisms, giving SubstitutionEquations. K-flatness is invariant under isomorphism by tensoring an acyclic test with that isomorphism; termwise flatness is invariant by the natural isomorphism of tensor-right functors. Apply the resolving equivalence of section_kflat_tensor_comparison to the termwise inverse image, using the equivalence counit. Finally use epsilon-naturality and cancel the two inverse unit transports to obtain UnitSubstitution.

The concrete argument uses the retained termwise functor data and the stored forward conjugation map; all comparison values are unchanged.

Step 1 writes out the gamma/eta/epsilon/kappa/h compatibility of pushpull-normalization. Step 2 uses the Y-normalization (inverse form) with naturality of epsilon at t and of gamma at the inverse of r^i. Step 3 checks that U=F_iA and W=F_iB are resolving, using 0G7E preservation of FP, the isomorphism h_A and reflection. It then uses the X-normalization, naturality of r^s at h_A,h_B, naturality of theta_X at the eta maps, and Step 1. Step 4 is the conjugation chain equation of oplax-total-comparison, localized and combined with kappa-naturality, and needs no flatness. Step 5 is the unit clause, kappa- and epsilon-naturality, and Step 1 at R_Y[0]. FIX: the first display of Step 3, r^s d_out G_X(r^i) = (d_A⊗d_B)theta_X, does not typecheck, because the target of G(r^i) is G(qU⊗qW) while the source of d_out is G q Tot(U⊗W). I replaced it with r^s d_out = (d_A⊗d_B) theta_X G_X(r^i), which the surrounding text and the rearrangement use.
